detect.doc: Identifies OpenAIAgents by its own scope and attribute namespace. Logfire's instrumentation records the SDK's spans under its own `logfire.openai_agents` scope and with Logfire's attributes, so the scope is the evidence that the spans describe this framework rather than Logfire itself: placed ahead of Logfire's detection, and the overlap is declared rather than left to priority.
detect.label: OpenAIAgents

alternatives.doc: The SDK's default service name on a span Logfire's instrumentation wrote. Logfire records the SDK's run-level spans without its `logfire.openai_agents` scope, so there the service name is the evidence that they describe this framework; ahead of Logfire's own detection for that reason, and only together with Logfire's signals, because on its own a service name is weak.
The service names the SDK reports by default, on their own. Weak evidence - a user names their own service - so it sits behind every instrumentation library's own signal.

messages.doc: The OpenAI Agents SDK records a local function execution as a Logfire span with the callable name and its JSON input. It carries no semantic-convention call id, so the name and arguments are retained and query-time correlation joins it to the oldest unmatched model call of that name.
The return value on the same local function span. Keeping the execution span's own result closes the tool call/result pair even though the next model request also replays that result as history.
The whole API response is recorded, and the tools it was called with are inside it.

span_facts.doc: The SDK's local function span uses Logfire's stable template and carries the callable name plus both sides of the execution.
